recipes.name: Cheese's Baked Macaroni and Cheese
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package fully cooked kielbasa sausage, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1 (10 ounce) package sharp Cheddar cheese, cubed
salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 cup dry bread crumbs, or more as needed

steps.text: Cook and stir the cut-up kielbasa in a large skillet over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until heated through and beginning to brown. Remove the sausage from the skillet, and set aside.

Fill a pan with lightly salted water, bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stir in the macaroni, and return to a boil. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through but is still firm to the bite, about 8 minutes. Drain well.
Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.

Melt the butter in the skillet over medium-low heat, and cook and stir the chopped onion for about 5 minutes, until translucent. Whisk in the flour, stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Cook and stir the butter, onion and flour for 2 to 3 minutes to make a roux, and remove from the heat. Whisk in the milk a little at a time, stirring constantly, until all the milk has been incorporated, and return to low heat. Bring the sauce to a simmer, and cook over low heat for about 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to finish cooking the flour. Whisk in the Cheddar cheese, a few cubes at a time, until all the cheese has been incorporated and the sauce is hot and smooth.
Pour the macaroni into the cheese sauce, and stir to combine. Stir in the cooked kielbasa, salt, and pepper.

Spoon the macaroni mixture into the prepared baking dish, and sprinkle the bread crumbs over the top. Bake for about 20 minutes in the preheated oven, until the crumbs are brown and the casserole is bubbling. Let stand for 15 minutes after baking, to set before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheese's Baked Macaroni and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: Homemade macaroni and cheese, baked with sliced kielbasa sausage, makes a warming weeknight supper.

review.reviewBody: My family loved this. I only used half of onion, added 1 tsp of ground mustard, used 1 cup half/half - 1 cup milk. Used 1/2 cup panko bread crumbs mixed with melted butter for the topping. Adding the Kielbasa makes this very filling, added a salad and that was dinner. Only 3 of us and had enough leftovers for the next night. Will be making again. Thanks

I used Tofurkey Kielbasa for this recipe and it was delicious!

Like other reviewers, I only added half a small onion, and I let it cook in the butter for longer than 5 minutes. I also added a little bit of garlic powder with the onions before the flour.

I used a little bit more than 8oz of elbow macaroni, and piled the mac n cheese into a 6X13 pan to change the crispy to gooey ratio. I also, like others, only added about 1/4 cup of breadcrumbs which I also dusted with Parmesan cheese. This was a big hit at the mac n cheese party I brought it to and I'll definitely make it again! Maybe with spicy Chipotle sausages and adobo peppers.

I've had this recipe in my favorites and made a version of it a few times a year since 2010 or so. My current adaptation has turned it from a "baked" mac & cheese to a crockpot version. As long as I've made it I've also subbed bacon for the kielbasa (I should actually use sausage one of these days!). I usually use a bit less than a full white onion. And now, reading some of the reviews, I may try and include some half & half in the Thanksgiving iteration!

The first time I made this, it was a little dry and needed more flavor, so I added about 1 cup of extra milk, a diced garlic clove, 1 tsp ground mustard, a little more shredded cheddar, a little shredded parmesan and 4oz of cream cheese to the sauce (for good measure). I allowed the sauce to simmer much longer than 2 minutes (6-8 minutes) and I continually tasted it to make sure it was flavorful and that the cheese was fully melted. Instead of using lots of breadcrumbs on top, I sprinkled more shredded cheddar and just used some Panko crumbs sparingly. I basically added 16oz of cheddar cheese (instead of 10oz) when it was all said and done! My boyfriend thought it was about the best thing he'd ever eaten!

Huge hit! Doubled recipe. I used 8 Tbs butter, sauteed onions, added double flour and milk. Added 2/3 block of 3lb cheddar cheese cubed and 4 oz velveta, stir till melted and the rest being same. For topping I used almost 1/2 bag Pepridge Farms herb bread crumb stuffing mixed with 1 stick melted butter. Spread on top. Baked 25 min at 350 then let it sit out of oven for 15 minutes. Excellent recipe. I never made homemade Mac and cheese before.
*********************
OK, so I have made this about 4 more times since above review. Each time I make it everyone says it is even better than last time. Once leftovers are gone (it makes more than 4 people can eat---2 servings each--at once) by a day or two later I am wondering if it's too soon to cook it again. It is awesome. This time I cooked mixture longer over higher heat, constantly stirring and I feel like it was even thicker. Haven't added kielbasa each time because I havent' had it on hand. LOVE this recipe. Over and out.

The absolute best way to cook sausage is to slice in 2 inch pieces and place in a pressure cooker with 3 cups of water. Cook about 25 minutes, when cool, remove the lid and drain all the fat . It's amazing how tender and lean the sausage becomes. After that use in your favorite recipes.

Just what I needed for supper tonight! We're huge cheese lovers, so I used about 16 oz of shredded cheddar & jack cheeses.
Also, for the bread crumbs, I always make my own by lightly toasting a few slices of bread and buttering them on both sides, before crumbling atop the macaroni. Some other users might want to try that, if they don't like the dry bread crumbs.
Additionally, this can be made with whole wheat flour, instead of white flour, if desired. We tried it that way and it still tasted great.

Really enjoyed it though I did make some alterations to it at the get go. I used extra sharp chedder instead of just sharp. I added a 1/4 teaspoon of liquid smoke and I didn't remember bread crumbs so I sprinkle more shredded cheese and for the last 5 minutes turn the oven on broiler high to get a nice crust.

I used Italian sausage which I cooked, then added the onion and set this aside. I made the roux in the same pan, deglazing with the butter but white wine would be good too. I also added about 2 teaspoons of prepared mustard. Hubby is fussy, and he went back for more. That is a win in my books!

This was super yummy but here are a few things I did differently. I am a mom, work and go to school, so speed is the name of the game. While some things I do believe need to take time, I think some processes here can be sped up. So 1. I made sure to use the smallest onion I had after reading reviews. 2. I cooked my pasta al dente so it wouldn't need 20 minute bake time @350. 3. After incorporating over low heat, I brought temp up to a med-med high and added the pasta/kielbasa mix, salt and peppered, got up to hot temp. And finally 4. I topped with bread crumbs (I did not measure, I just dusted as there were complaints of the bread crumbs soaking up too much of the sauce) and then broiled it until brown and crispy. I think the broil function is a vastly underused feature. Viola. We all loved it, hubby was mad there wasn't more left when he got home from work :)

I make this with Barilla Veggie elbow macaroni to throw in a serving of hidden veggies. This is a kid and adult frienly recipe that I go to often. I usally make it ahead of time and just pop it in the oven on a busy night.
I added home fried potatoes, pinto beans, and sauteed celery. The cheese sauce is the best I've made so far. Delicious!
I used 3 kinds of cheese and cubed ham instead of kielbasa. Also added dry mustard and chili powder to sauce.
Loved this, as did the whole family. The recipe is flexible too. I threw in some cauliflower and spinach too in order to add some veg and make a complete dinner. Will make again.

I lost my basic mac and cheese recipe years ago. I've tried one since that had garlic??? in it and it was horrible! I found this today and made it. My husband never has seconds, but he filled up his plate both times and told me he loves it! It's a keeper for me!
It was a little off in amounts. I used 2 cups of pasta and increased the flour by 1 Tbl and the cheese to 2 cups of shredded cheese ( a blend ).

This turned out delicious. I was surprised that you made the cheese sauce with the onions already cooked in the butter. I think it added a taste that I hadn't had in other recipes. The kielbasa was great .
